newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr edges up vs yen following Greenspan remarks.
newsitem.headline: Dlr edges up vs yen following Greenspan remarks.

text.p: 0131 GMT --*Dollar inched up in mid-morning Tokyo on short-covering by traders partly due to Fed Chairman Greenspan's comments, which market took to mean further rise in U.S. interest rates may be possible.

*Some importer purchases seen, along with some short-covering by U.S. banks, but Japanese investors were said to be sidelined so far in morning trade. *Earlier, greenback fell vs yen due to comments by Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka that Japan hopes G7 agreement on currencies will be further digested by markets.

*Greenspan said in speech delivered to New York University that he expects economic growth to slow later this year and into next, but added that central bank would need to act if that does not prove to be the case.
*Greenspan said: "Should the expected slowing in the growth of demand fail to materialise, we would need to address any emerging pressures in product and credit markets."
*A trust bank dealer said, "His commnets led to some dollar buying by traders to cover short positions built up earlier. U.S. bank short-covering was also detected."

*Earlier, dollar was dragged down towards 123 yen after Mistuzuka's comments encouraged traders to sell dollars for yen. Mitsuzuka said: "The content (of the G7 agreement) has gradually filtered through to the markets. However, we are not satisfied with that and hope the impact of the G7 agreement will be further digested by the markets. I will not comment on the issue of currency intervention."
*A city bank dealer said, "The market is really nervous and sensitive to officials' comments."
*Near-term support expected near 123.00 yen, followed by 122.80 yen, but downward risk still remains, dealers said.

*Dollar weaker and slipping towards 123 yen in early Tokyo as sales emerged, mainly from interbank dealers, on back of article in Japan financial daily Nikkei Kinyu speculating on chance of Japan's official discount rate being raised in July.

*Article suggested that some in Bank of Japan (BOJ) may be of opinion that Japan's low interest rate policy should come to end soon. But dollar already under pressure early in Asian trade, when sales overseas may have triggered options-linked stop-loss sales under 123.50 yen, dealers said. --- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3432-8584
